provenance: Written on 2026-11-05 from Ifirma::postProcessConfiguration() as of commit d708c46 and confirmed by running it, before the IfirmaSettings table replaced its checks (refactor-srp-splits 7.2). 'valid' is the request the settings form sends when everything is right, and the Configuration::updateValue() calls the save makes for it, in order, type for type. It also posts IFIRMA_KEY_RACHUNEK (the form got its input in the 1.5.0 review fixes): the save writes that key even when a request leaves it out (trim(false) gives ''). An odd-length hex key is refused since then, an API key being whole bytes. The 'minimal request' scenario shows the real shape: a request with only the fields the checks need still gets every call, each key written from what the save makes of its missing field. A scenario changes that request ('change'; a null removes the field) or replaces it ('post'), and lists the calls it must cause ('writes') or only those whose value differs from the valid ones ('writes_as_valid'). A request with a validation error writes nothing. 'notice' is what the page shows above the form. 'page_writes' lists the calls the page makes after a successful save; the default is none: since the limit box stopped reading iFirma on every view (add-api-usage-delivery-retry-status-filter-and-ci-fix 3.8) the page writes nothing, where it used to stamp IFIRMA_RATE_WINDOW and IFIRMA_RATE_DAY_WINDOW for an even-length hex abonent key. A value {"repeat": s, "times": n} stands for s repeated n times. Change this file only when the settings behaviour is changed on purpose.
